title: Anthropic shares decline following initial public offering
dek: Anthropic shares experienced a significant decline following the company's record-breaking Nasdaq debut, as broader technology market sell-offs and investor profit-taking pressured the stock price.
happened: Anthropic launched its initial public offering on 19 November, pricing shares at $83 and raising $81.3 billion. The stock opened at $111.50 before closing its first day of trading at $97.17. By 20 November, shares fell more than 10% amid a broader technology market downturn, briefly touching $83.05 before recovering slightly above $86. According to market reports, the decline was influenced by investors seeking quick profits and a general sell-off in artificial intelligence stocks. NYU Stern professor Aswath Damodaran noted that Anthropic's aggressive infrastructure commitments, including estimated compute lease debts of nearly $500 billion, present potential liabilities if revenue growth does not meet expectations. Damodaran, who valued the company at $77 per share, stated that the proximity of the IPO price to his valuation made him uncomfortable. Meanwhile, the Nasdaq index experienced a decline of more than 4% on 20 November, contributing to the downward pressure on Anthropic's share price.

sides.says: The company completed the largest initial public offering in history, raising $81.3 billion at an offer price of $83 per share.
The valuation expert estimated the company's value at $77 per share, citing concerns over compute costs and regulatory drag. He stated that the IPO price being close to his estimate "terrifies" him.
Analysts attributed the share price volatility to a broader technology sector sell-off, investor profit-taking, and concerns regarding the company's high infrastructure spending requirements.

next: Market participants continue to monitor the stock's performance amid broader technology sector volatility and the company's long-term revenue growth trajectory.
summary: Anthropic's shares have declined following its record-breaking initial public offering on 19 November. After opening significantly above its $83 offer price, the stock faced downward pressure due to a wider technology market sell-off and investor profit-taking. Analysts have raised concerns regarding the company's high infrastructure costs and the sustainability of its growth trajectory. While the company achieved a trillion-dollar valuation on its first day, subsequent trading sessions saw the share price approach its initial offering level.
